root_cause.text: The secure storage access exception handler incorrectly assumed that pages without PG_arch_1 (donated memory) are already accessible, causing arch_make_folio_accessible() to become a no-op and never resolving the access exception, leading to infinite loops.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The secure storage access exception handler incorrectly assumed that pages without PG_arch_1 (donated memory) are already accessible, causing arch_make_folio_accessible() to become a no-op and never resolving the access exception, leading to infinite loops.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix improper handling of secure memory accesses by replacing BUG() with proper error handling and updating the conversion mechanism.
intent_record.what: Replaced call to arch_make_folio_accessible with uv_convert_from_secure and added clearing of PG_arch_1 flag on success; changed error handling from BUG() to handle_fault_error_nolock when conversion fails; added comment explaining valid fixup types for kernel accesses to donated secure memory.
intent_record.how: Instead of panicking on failed secure page conversion, the kernel now handles the fault gracefully by returning an error via handle_fault_error_nolock, allowing fixups like zeropad to proceed. The conversion is done via uv_convert_from_secure and the PG_arch_1 flag is cleared to indicate accessibility.

grouping_result.intent: Fix improper handling of secure memory accesses by replacing BUG() with proper error handling and updating the conversion mechanism.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the handling of secure memory accesses, replacing BUG() with proper error handling, which corresponds to the exception handler that incorrectly assumed pages without PG_arch_1 are accessible.

candidates.rationale: The call to arch_make_folio_accessible() on pages without PG_arch_1 (donated memory) returns 0 without actually making the page accessible, causing the access exception to never be resolved and leading to an infinite loop.

vuln_statements.explanation: The call to arch_make_folio_accessible() returns 0 on pages without PG_arch_1 (donated memory) without actually making the page accessible, causing the access exception to never be resolved and leading to an infinite loop.

Author: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 22 14:06:00 2024 +0200

    s390/mm: Get rid of fault type switch statements
    
    With GMAP_FAULT fault type gone, there are only KERNEL_FAULT and
    USER_FAULT fault types left. Therefore there is no need for any fault
    type switch statements left.
    
    Rename get_fault_type() into is_kernel_fault() and let it return a
    boolean value. Change all switch statements to if state
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit refactors do_secure_storage_access() by replacing a switch statement with an if-else, but preserves the same vulnerable logic: calling arch_make_folio_accessible() without ensuring that it actually makes the page accessible (as described in the root cause, it becomes a no-op for pages without PG_arch_1). The kernel fault path (lines 439-446 in the new code) still calls arch_make_folio_accessible() and does not add any check to prevent infinite loops, so the vulnerability remains unaddressed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function includes a check for TEID bit 61 (lines 802-819) and the misc UV feature, which prevents infinite loops by sending SIGSEGV or panicking when the address is invalid.
